# v0.1.8 preview

This artifact is a preview. It is not a claim of GitHub Actions
equivalence.

The version string is 0.1.8. The capability version is 12.

Job containers use Docker network `none` by default.
`worker --network bridge` opts in to egress. Service containers start
only with that opt-in. A host that upgrades onto a tree where the
job network defaults to `none` adds `--network bridge` on that
host's unit when jobs need egress. Cargo and pip need it. The
repository unit omits the flag.

A job container is created with `--security-opt no-new-privileges`
and `--cap-drop ALL`. Passwordless sudo is off unless the worker is
started with `--passwordless-sudo`.

A bash or sh run script quotes each expression. An expression in
`eval` or in a shell `-c` command is refused. A pull request that
changes a workflow file is refused. A missing pull request author
association is refused.

Every engine call uses the Docker context named `default` unless
`worker --docker-context` or `ROOKRUNNER_DOCKER_CONTEXT` names one.
An inherited `DOCKER_CONTEXT` or `DOCKER_HOST` does not select the
engine.

A host copy of the worker unit must set `NoNewPrivileges=yes`.
The repository unit sets that directive. A copy that omits it is
reported by systemd as `NoNewPrivileges=no` and must be set to `yes`.

The acceptance platform is Linux x86_64. Other platforms are not
claimed. The acceptance interpreter is Python 3.12. The package
requires Python 3.11 or newer.

PyYAML 6.0.3 is installed with the wheel and is not vendored.

The wheel and the source tarball can be built from this tree. They
are not published. This file does not create a tag.

The worker has no listen socket. The one write grant the planner
accepts is `id-token: write`. Every other write stays rejected.

A poll pass keeps going when an older claimed run has no readable
snapshot. That run is skipped and later runs still post.

Passwordless sudo still drops every capability. It then keeps
`SETUID`, `SETGID`, `AUDIT_WRITE`, `CHOWN`, `DAC_OVERRIDE`,
`DAC_READ_SEARCH`, and `FOWNER`. Root in that job can chown and
chmod the apt partial directories, unlink a file in a mode-0700
directory owned by another user, and stat a mode-0700 workspace
owned by the job user. A job without that opt-in still sets
no-new-privileges and adds no capabilities.

Rookrunner can act as an OIDC issuer for jobs. Signing keys are RSA
files of at least 2048 bits under `oidc/` in the key directory.
`oidc publish` writes the discovery document and the public key set
for the issuer host. Only the public key members are written.

A per-job token endpoint runs only when the worker is started with
`worker --oidc-issuer`. That flag is off by default, and startup
refuses when the active signing key is missing, unreadable, or
below 2048 bits. A job must grant `id-token: write`. The run must
be trusted: a fork, an override run, and a run the secret allowlist
does not match receive no token. A same-repository pull request
also needs `worker --oidc-pull-request`. A job that passes gets
`ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`
in every step, and trades them for a token that lives for five
minutes. A job that does not pass runs without them, and the
refusal is audited. Jobs that use a token need `--network bridge`.
Each mint and each refusal is one line in `oidc-audit.jsonl`,
without the token.

A pre-commit hook rejects an unformatted staged Python file under
`src/` or `tests/`. `scripts/install-hooks.sh` points a clone at
the hook.

The project license is the MIT License.

The App private key is not in the artifact.
